title: Open-weight coding model tops 85 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 by Q4 2026
body: GLM-5.2's fully-open MIT release lands at 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro, trailing the closed frontier's 85.0 by roughly four points while undercutting it on price-performance and already wiring into 20-plus coding environments. Each open-weight generation from the Chinese coding-model labs has closed a chunk of that gap rather than holding station, and the surrounding serving stack is removing the deployment tax that kept these models off local hardware: vLLM v0.23.0 promotes its faster execution path to default for dense models, and MosaicQuant's unified 4-bit scheme reports near-FP16 accuracy, making large MoE weights cheaper to run yourself. The prediction is that a permissively-licensed (MIT or Apache-2.0) open-weight model reaches or exceeds 85.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 on vendor-reported scores, erasing the headline coding gap to the closed leader. The score is benchmark-specific and falsifiable; independent replication and production latency remain the open caveats, but the trajectory points at parity on this metric within two quarters.

summary: GLM-5.2's open MIT weights reached 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 versus 85.0 for the closed frontier, narrowing the coding gap each release while cheaper 4-bit serving lowers the cost of running them locally. Expect a permissively-licensed open-weight model to reach 85.0 on that benchmark by Q4 2026.
